title: To build the Statue of Liberty, every part of an 11 m model was copied four times larger
body: On 28 October 2026 the Statue of Liberty marked 140 years since it was [unveiled in New York Harbor](https://www.nps.gov/stli/learn/historyculture/places_creating_statue.htm), on 28 October 1886, and an exhibition on the Eiffel Tower marks the anniversary until 12 November. The French sculptor Auguste Bartholdi didn’t carve his statue: he enlarged it. According to the US [National Park Service](https://npshistory.com/handbooks/historical/11/hh11e.htm), a study model 1.25 m high led to one of 2.85 m and then to an 11 m model, corrected down to the smallest detail; that model was cut into sections, and each was made again four times its size, with about 9,000 measurements for each section. Carpenters built wooden molds of the full-size pieces, and more than 300 copper sheets, 3/32 of an inch or about 2.4 mm thick, were hammered into them by hand. A thin skin made sense, because the material had to be light: four times taller means 16 times the surface, but 64 times the volume. Inside, Gustave Eiffel’s iron pylon holds each sheet up on its own iron strap.

slides.question: The Statue of Liberty’s skin is made of hammered copper sheets. How thick are they, in millimetres?
slides.explanation: About 2.4 mm, 3/32 of an inch: “the thickness of two pennies placed together”, says the US National Park Service.

slides.alt: Animation on a dark harbour night: a copper silhouette of the Statue of Liberty, 46 m tall; plaster models of 1.25, 2.85 and 11 m beside a person; a section copied four times larger with measuring points; a square growing 16 times, a cube 64 times; copper hammered into a mold; Eiffel’s pylon.

slides.prompt: Enlarge Bartholdi’s 1.25 m study model until it is as tall as the Statue of Liberty, 46 m from base to torch.
slides.takeaway: About 37 times taller: its skin is about 1,360 times the model’s surface, and a solid copy would hold about 50,000 times its volume. That is why the statue is a copper skin 2.4 mm thick.

slides.heading: Bartholdi’s models and the Statue of Liberty, by height
slides.note: US National Park Service. The statue measured from the top of its base to the torch.

events.text: Arrives in New York Harbor in crates

slides.question: Why did each section of the Statue of Liberty, copied four times larger, need 16 times as much copper skin?
options: The copper was four times thicker
slides.explanation: Area grows with the square of the size: 4 × 4 = 16. Volume grows with the cube, 64 times, which is why the statue is a thin copper skin on an iron frame.
